key_insight: OSReward shows that current VLM-based judges for computer-use agent trajectories are not yet reliable, with a strong tendency to be overly lenient and misclassify failures as successes.
engineering_relevance: The paper provides a practical path to low-cost, scalable reward modeling for computer-use agents, enabling more trustworthy evaluation, data curation, and RL training across platforms.
method: Built OSReward, a cross-platform benchmark of human-verified CUA trajectories with ground-truth verdicts from multi-stage annotation.
Created OSReward-Hard for genuinely difficult judgments and OSReward-Multi for fine-grained efficiency/alignment scoring.
Trained OS-Shepherd-100K and resulting OS-Shepherd reward models (9B/35B) as open, reasoning-annotated judges.
evidence_signal: The benchmark evaluation spans diverse agent backbones and shows even state-of-the-art VLM judges still fall short of ideal reliability, with systematic leniency bias.
watch_item: Performance depends on high-quality trajectory annotations and careful judge calibration; the most reliable frontier models are still costly, so deployment tradeoffs matter.
paper_title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
